title: Gender Studies
subtitle: Optional Subject · CSS 2026
answerKeyNote: Practice answer key (not an official FPSC key). Review carefully.

questions.text: Judith Butler's concept of "performativity" argues that gender is not an internal reality but:

options.A: A biological destiny determined by chromosomal patterns
options.B: A stylized repetition of acts sanctioned by social norms
options.C: A fixed psychological archetype inherited from ancestors

questions.text: The term "Glass Cliff" refers to:

options.A: The invisible barrier preventing women from rising to top ranks
options.B: The phenomenon where women are promoted to leadership roles during periods of crisis or downturn, increasing the risk of failure
options.C: The rapid promotion of men in female-dominated professions

questions.explanation: Ryan & Haslam (2005). (A is the glass ceiling; C the glass escalator.)

questions.text: In the context of Gender and Development (GAD), the "practical gender needs" differ from "strategic gender interests" in that the former:

options.A: Challenge the subordinate position of women in society
options.B: Focus exclusively on legislative quotas and political representation
options.C: Address immediate necessities (water, shelter, food) without challenging labor divisions

questions.text: Michel Foucault's "History of Sexuality" challenges the "repressive hypothesis" by suggesting that:

options.A: The Victorian era successfully silenced all discourse on sexuality
options.B: Sexuality is a purely biological drive independent of power structures
options.C: Power produces discourse on sexuality rather than just repressing it

questions.text: The "Patriarchal Bargain," a concept explaining why women might uphold patriarchal norms to maximize their own security, was elaborated by:
Which wave of feminism is most closely associated with the slogan "The Personal is Political"?
The notion that men suffer from "hegemonic masculinity," which restricts their emotional expression and forces them into dominance hierarchies, is attributed to:
Which UN Conference on Women resulted in the "Platform for Action," a key agenda for women's empowerment?
questions.explanation: Beijing Declaration and Platform for Action.

questions.text: The concept of "Strategic Essentialism" suggests that:

options.A: Gender differences are biological and unchangeable
options.B: Minority groups may temporarily act as if their identities are stable to achieve political goals
options.C: Essentialist arguments should never be used in feminist discourse

questions.text: "Standpoint Theory" argues that:

options.A: All knowledge is objective and neutral
options.B: Science should be abandoned as a patriarchal tool
options.C: Knowledge stems from social position, and marginalized groups offer a more complete perspective

questions.text: Elisabeth Schüssler Fiorenza coined the term kyriarchy to describe:

options.B: Interlocking structures of domination such as gender, race and class

questions.text: The "WID" (Women in Development) approach, which emerged in the 1970s, was primarily criticized for:

options.B: Ignoring the economic contribution of women completely

questions.explanation: WID was criticized for adding women to existing development without challenging gender relations.

questions.text: Which Pakistani legislation criminalized "Honour Killings" and closed the loophole of family forgiveness?
The "Bargaining with Patriarchy" concept explains how women strategize within constraints. This term was coined by:
Which UN Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) specifically targets "Gender Equality"?
The reformist movement in the subcontinent that advocated for women's education and opposed Sati was led by:
questions.explanation: Raja Ram Mohan Roy (Brahmo Samaj) — not listed.

questions.text: "Doing Gender," a sociological perspective viewing gender as an accomplished interactional display, was proposed by:
The "Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women" (CEDAW) is often described as:

options.A: An international bill of rights for women

questions.text: "Sticky Floor" refers to:

options.A: Women stuck in low-wage, low-mobility jobs
options.B: High retention rates of female employees

questions.text: The concept of "Matrix of Domination" was developed by:
